A.depoimento: Our armies have marched on Santarem to claim it for the crown. Building more archers will ensure our dominance in the region. Victory is within our grasp!
A.plano: We will attack the neutral village of Santarem to expand our territory. I am building an archer to strengthen our forces for next turn. We must hold Santarem to increase our resource production.

B.depoimento: I have ordered my armies to march on Tarragona and Girona. With the current forces, I expect to capture both neutral villages and begin my expansion across the map. I am also building more spearman to ensure my capital remains secure.
B.plano: Capture Tarragona and Girona to expand my territory and open up the road network. Build spearman to replenish ranks and secure the capital. Explore newly connected villages next turn.

A.depoimento: I ordered the conquest of Coimbra to expand my kingdom. I also built archers in Lisbon to prepare for future battles.
A.plano: Attack Coimbra with all troops from Santarem to expand territory. Build 2 archers in Lisboa to strengthen the army. Next turn, assess losses and reinforce Coimbra if needed, then continue expansion.

B.depoimento: I split my forces in Tarragona to assault both Castellon and Zaragoza simultaneously, sending archers and knights to each target while leaving a spearman to hold the village. From Barcelona, I dispatched two spearmen and a knight to reinforce Girona, setting up next turn's attack on Huesca. I also ordered two new spearmen built in the capital to replenish my ranks after the coming battles.
B.plano: Taking Castellon and Zaragoza this turn with split forces from Tarragona. Reinforcing Girona with troops from Barcelona to prepare for the attack on Huesca next turn. After these battles, I will have 5 villages. Next turn: launch the Huesca assault, explore newly revealed villages around Castellon/Zaragoza, and continue building troops in Barcelona and Tarragona as resources allow.

A.depoimento: Our armies move on Evora and Porto! With the main force striking Porto and archers taking Evora, we expand our kingdom. The neutral villages will fall, and our strength will grow.
A.plano: Conquer Evora and Porto this turn to expand our territory and economy. Lisboa sends archers to Evora; Coimbra launches its full army at Porto. We build spearman in Lisboa and Santarem to start rebuilding our forces. Next turn, we will assess losses, reinforce our new villages, and plan attacks on Badajoz, Salamanca, and beyond.

B.depoimento: My armies assault Huesca today, led by Girona's finest. I'm building knights and archers to strengthen my forces. Reinforcements are marching to prepare for the next wave of conquests. The kingdom grows, but I must move swiftly to secure victory.
B.plano: Taking Huesca this turn with Girona's full force. Building knights and archers in Barcelona, Tarragona, and Girona. Reinforcing Girona with Barcelona's troops and Castellon with Tarragona's spearman for next turn's attacks. After Huesca, focus on Valencia and exploring new territories. Need to expand quickly to reach 18 villages.

A.depoimento: The king's armies advance on all fronts! Porto's legions assault Salamanca, Lisboa's troops reinforce Evora, and Santarem's spearman march to Coimbra. Our forges produce a knight, spearman, and archers as we push our expansion.
A.plano: Attack Salamanca with Porto's full army to secure a key hub and open the route to Madrid. Send Lisboa's troops to Evora to prepare an attack on Faro next turn. Move Santarem's spearman to Coimbra to concentrate forces near the new frontier. Build a knight in Lisboa, spearman in Santarem, and archer in Coimbra to rebuild our army. Next turn, we will assault Faro from Evora and Badajoz from Salamanca, while continuing to build.

B.depoimento: Our armies are on the move! We are launching a coordinated strike on four neutral villages. Castellon will take Valencia, Zaragoza will crush Madrid, Huesca will capture Pamplona, and we already prepare for Teruel. Reinforcements are flowing across our borders as we speak.
B.plano: Turn 4 setup for capturing four neutrals. Castellon builds archer and receives Tarragona's archer to enable Valencia attack; also builds spearman for Teruel next turn. Zaragoza builds spearman and receives Huesca's spearman to overwhelm Madrid. Huesca sends spearman away and receives Girona's archer to become archer-heavy for Pamplona. Turn 5: Castellon sends archers to Valencia and prepares spearman for Teruel; Zaragoza sends main force to Madrid; Huesca sends archers to Pamplona. Reinforce captured villages with remaining troops.

A.depoimento: We launched a powerful assault from Salamanca against the neutral city of Badajoz, aiming to consolidate our western holdings and secure the route to the south. Meanwhile, we began shifting our forces, sending our knight from Lisbon to Evora to prepare for an upcoming strike on Faro. Our builders worked tirelessly, producing new spearman and archers across our villages to replenish our ranks and prepare for the next phase of our campaign.
A.plano: Attack Badajoz from Salamanca with all troops to secure the link with Santarem. Send Lisboa's knight to Evora to prepare for the attack on Faro next turn. Build spearman in Santarem, Coimbra, Porto, archer in Evora, and knight in Lisboa to rebuild our army and reinforce the frontier.

B.depoimento: My lords, the time has come to strike! I have ordered Castellon, Zaragoza, and Huesca to launch simultaneous assaults on the neutral territories of Valencia, Madrid, and Pamplona. Our troops are optimized for victory: spearmen lead the charge to counter their knights, while archers provide deadly support. By capturing these three villages, we secure our borders and bring our total to nine. I have also ordered our blacksmiths to work through the night, building knights and archers to replenish our ranks for the next phase of our campaign.
B.plano: Capture Valencia, Madrid, and Pamplona this turn. Castellon attacks Valencia with all available troops (3 spearman, 3 archer) to overcome the 8 defense. Zaragoza attacks Madrid with its full force (4 spearman, 1 archer, 1 knight) utilizing the spearman-knight counter for 1.5x damage. Huesca attacks Pamplona with 2 archer and 1 knight, using archer-spearman counter. Build knights and archers in our villages to replenish forces for the next turn's expansion towards Teruel and beyond.

A.depoimento: While my army takes Badajoz, I attack Faro and reinforce Salamanca. I build knights and spearmen to grow my army for the next campaigns.
A.plano: Attack Faro with all Evora troops. Reinforce Salamanca with Porto's spearmen and Coimbra's archer/spearmen. Send Lisboa's knight to Evora. Build knights in interior villages, spearman in Salamanca. Next turn: garrison Badajoz, move on Toledo/Sevilha, keep Santarem's spearmen in reserve.

B.depoimento:
We are building up our knight forces and moving them to the front lines.
Madrid's garrison marches on the empty Salamanca to capture it.
Knights from Barcelona, Tarragona, and Zaragoza are sent to reinforce Madrid and Pamplona for the coming attacks on Toledo and Burgos.
B.plano:
Build knights in rear villages and send them to Madrid and Pamplona.
Madrid sends all troops to capture empty Salamanca.
Next turn, attack Toledo with 3 knights from Madrid and Burgos with 2 knights from Pamplona.
Do not attack other villages yet.

A.depoimento: I ordered Badajoz to attack Salamanca with archers and a knight, aiming to finish the enemy garrison after my spearmen weaken it. At the same time, I sent Santarem's spearmen to reinforce Badajoz. I also built new troops across my villages to prepare for the next expansion into Toledo and the east.
A.plano: Focus on taking Salamanca with Badajoz's archers and knight, while Santarem's spearmen reinforce Badajoz. Build knights and archers in interior villages. Next turn, after Salamanca falls, move on Toledo from Badajoz. Keep Coimbra and Porto defended. Watch for enemy movements from Madrid.

B.depoimento: This turn, I am reinforcing our frontline at Salamanca by sending three knights from Madrid to join the garrison and repel the incoming enemy army. Simultaneously, I am sending two knights from Pamplona to capture the neutral village of Burgos, expanding our territory and bringing us closer to our goal of holding 18 villages. I am also ordering a massive production of knights and archers across our villages to ensure our army grows steadily.
B.plano: Reinforce Salamanca with 3 knights from Madrid to defend against the incoming enemy army. Send 2 knights from Pamplona to capture Burgos. Build knights in Barcelona, Girona, Castellon, and Salamanca, and archers in other villages to grow the army. Focus on holding the western front and expanding into neutral territories.

A.depoimento: I have ordered a strong spearman assault from Badajoz to retake Salamanca, the enemy-held village that has changed hands too many times. I am also sending a knight from Santarem to reinforce Coimbra's defenses. Across my realm, I am building archers and knights to grow my army, preparing to conquer the neutral villages of Vigo and Sevilha in the coming turns.
A.plano: Attack Salamanca with 6 spearman from Badajoz to reclaim the village and secure the northern border. Reinforce Coimbra with a knight from Santarem to protect against enemy counter-attacks. Build archers in Coimbra and Evora to prepare for the next pushes into Vigo and Sevilha, which require archers to counter their spearman garrisons.

B.depoimento: We focused on strengthening our core by building knights and archers in every village. Valencia's archers marched to capture Murcia, while a steady stream of reinforcements from the east flowed into Salamanca, ready to launch a major campaign next turn.
B.plano: Capture Murcia with Valencia's archers. Reinforce Salamanca heavily with knights from all eastern villages to prepare for next turn's offensive. Keep Salamanca's current troops for defense. Build knights and archers everywhere to grow the army.

A.depoimento: We launched a coordinated strike on Toledo, falling it with spearmen and knights from Badajoz. Simultaneously, we flooded our borders with reinforcements: Badajoz, Coimbra, Porto, and Faro all received fresh troops to blunt any enemy counterattack. Our builders worked tirelessly, producing archers and spearmen for the next phase of expansion.
A.plano: Attack Toledo from Badajoz with 2S 2K to gain a village and secure the northern front. Reinforce Badajoz with 1K from Santarem and 2A 1K from Faro to maintain defense after the attack. Reinforce Coimbra with 2K from Lisboa and Porto with 1A 2K from Coimbra to hold the western borders. Reinforce Faro with 2A 1K from Evora. Build archers and spearmen across all villages to replenish losses and prepare for attacks on Vigo and Sevilha next turn. Do not engage Salamanca; it is too heavily reinforced.

B.depoimento: This turn, I heavily reinforced Salamanca by sending the available knights from Madrid and Zaragoza to join the eight knights already marching there, creating a formidable defense. I built archers in every village and sent Valencia's entire force to capture Murcia, relying on the archer counter bonus to secure victory. My armies are expanding, and I aim to push westward next turn.
B.plano: Defend Salamanca against the incoming enemy army using the eight arriving knights plus reinforcements from Madrid and Zaragoza. Capture Murcia with Valencia's archers and spearmen, leveraging the counter bonus. Build archers and knights across all villages to grow the army. Next turn, if Salamanca holds, attack Teruel from Valencia/Zaragoza and Vigo from Burgos, and explore unexplored villages via Murcia.

A.depoimento: This turn, we launched offensives on three fronts: Sevilha from Faro, Vigo from Porto, and Madrid from Toledo. We reinforced our border villages of Badajoz and Coimbra with troops from Santarem, Lisboa, and Evora. We also moved troops from Faro to Badajoz to strengthen our southern defense. Our builders worked to produce knights and archers to refill our ranks.
A.plano: We are attacking Sevilha from Faro, Vigo from Porto, and Madrid from Toledo to gain villages and move toward 18. We sent reinforcements from Santarem to Badajoz, from Lisboa to Coimbra, and from Evora to Faro (to move later). We left small garrisons in Porto and Faro to support the offensives. We built knights and archers to replenish losses. Next turn, we will assess the battle results and continue expanding, likely targeting Cordoba and Teruel.

B.depoimento: Orders given: Valencia's archers march on Murcia to correct last turn's failure. Salamanca's mighty knight contingent strikes Coimbra to break the enemy's western flank, while a vanguard reinforces Madrid. The great build-up of archers continues across the realm. We strike hard and fast.
B.plano: Capture Murcia with Valencia's archers and Coimbra with Salamanca's knights. Reinforce Madrid with Zaragoza's archer and Salamanca's knight. Build archers across all villages to grow the army. Next turn, attack Toledo from Madrid, and explore Cordoba from Murcia.

A.depoimento: We are consolidating our forces for a decisive push south. We abandon the isolated northern villages to save their troops, and mass our army in Sevilha to take Cordoba. Our enemies may take some border villages, but we will expand into neutral territory and use it to retake our lands.
A.plano: Plan: Focus on Sevilha to attack Cordoba next turn. We moved Porto's garrison to Vigo and Santarem's knight to Badajoz to save troops. We built in secure villages. Expect to lose some border villages, but taking Cordoba opens the south and allows us to retake Toledo from there.

B.depoimento: I have ordered a three-pronged attack on the enemy villages of Toledo, Santarem, and Vigo, while simultaneously reinforcing my border villages of Madrid, Burgos, and Coimbra. My army is growing with the construction of archers across my realm. The time has come to expand and secure my borders.
B.plano: Attack Toledo, Santarem, and Vigo to expand my territory. Reinforce Madrid, Burgos, and Coimbra to secure borders. Build archers across all villages to grow the army. Next turn, assess the situation and plan attacks on Cordoba and Teruel, or explore the south.

A.depoimento: King A has ordered a grand offensive on multiple fronts! From the south, Sevilha's army marches on Cordoba. In the center, Badajoz's spearmen and knights strike at Toledo. In the north, Vigo's knights charge against Burgos, while also sending reinforcements to the undefended Porto. In the capital, Lisboa receives reinforcements from Evora, preparing for the next strike. Our armies are on the move, and the map shall be ours!
A.plano: We are launching a massive multi-front offensive this turn. Sevilha attacks Cordoba (neutral) to secure the south. Badajoz attacks Toledo to secure the center and connect with Cordoba. Vigo attacks Burgos to secure the north and turn Vigo into an interior village, while also sending reinforcements to Porto to defend it. Evora sends reinforcements to Lisboa to prepare for an attack on Santarem next turn. We build troops in all our villages to maintain our army strength.

B.depoimento: We launched a massive three-pronged attack to secure the victory. Our forces in Coimbra took Porto, Toledo's army captured Cordoba, and Santarem's knights and archers conquered the enemy capital Lisboa. With these three conquests, we now hold 18 villages, satisfying the win condition. We also reinforced our borders and continued building up our army across the empire.
B.plano: Attack Porto from Coimbra, Cordoba from Toledo, and Lisboa from Santarem to reach 18 villages. Build archers and knights in all villages to grow the army. Reinforce Toledo from Madrid and Coimbra from Salamanca to defend the borders after the attacks.

A.depoimento: This turn we strike south, taking Murcia to expand our kingdom. Our forces assault the enemy village while reinforcements march to our border cities and we build up our armies. We are preparing a major offensive for next turn to reclaim lost lands and push toward victory.
A.plano: Attack Murcia with all of Cordoba's troops to secure the south and expand our territory. Reinforce Lisboa from Evora, Badajoz from Faro, and Cordoba from Sevilha to prepare for next turn's attacks. Build troops in all possible villages to grow our army. Next turn, Lisboa will attack Santarem and Badajoz will attack Salamanca. We hold in the north and evaluate attacks on Madrid/Teruel after building up.

B.depoimento: I have sent my army from Porto to conquer the isolated enemy village of Vigo, which should be an easy victory. At the same time, I am reinforcing my border villages against potential enemy counter-attacks while building a large number of knights and archers to prepare for the next offensive. My goal is to reach 18 villages and secure the win.
B.plano: Conquer Vigo with the army from Porto to reach 16 villages. Reinforce Madrid, Murcia, Burgos, and Santarem against enemy counter-attacks. Build knights and archers everywhere to prepare for the next offensive. Next turn, assess the situation and consider attacking Badajoz or Teruel to reach 18 villages.

A.depoimento: We launched a double offensive this turn: Badajoz struck Salamanca, while Murcia attacked Valencia. We reinforced our capital Lisboa from Evora and consolidated our southern holdings by sending Cordoba's archer to Murcia and Sevilha's knight to Badajoz. Troops were built in all villages to expand our army. The conquest of Valencia gives us a foothold in the east, and taking Salamanca weakens the enemy's western flank.
A.plano: Attack Salamanca from Badajoz and Valencia from Murcia to expand our territory. Reinforce Lisboa from Evora, and send Cordoba's archer to Murcia, Sevilha's knight to Badajoz, and Faro's knight to Badajoz. Build troops in all villages to grow our army for future attacks on Santarem and Madrid.

A.depoimento: We launch a double strike on Santarem and Madrid to expand our territory, while reinforcing our border villages and building troops across the realm to prepare for the next phase of the campaign.
A.plano: Attack Santarem from Lisboa and Madrid from Toledo to expand our territory. Reinforce Valencia from Murcia, Badajoz from Faro and Sevilha, and Lisboa from Evora. Build troops in all villages to grow our army. Do not attack Castellon or Teruel yet as we lack the force.

B.depoimento: King B's forces moved to defend Salamanca from the enemy's assault, sending reinforcements from Madrid, Porto, and Coimbra. At the same time, we launched a double offensive, sending armies from Castellon to Valencia and from Santarem to Badajoz to conquer these key enemy villages. Our workers are busy building archers and knights across the kingdom to ensure our dominance on the battlefield.
B.plano: We are reinforcing Salamanca from Madrid, Porto, and Coimbra to defend against the incoming enemy army. We are attacking Valencia from Castellon and Badajoz from Santarem to conquer them and increase our village count to 16. We are building archers and knights in all our villages to grow our army for the next turns. We must hold the conquered villages for 2 consecutive turns to reach the 18-village threshold.

A.depoimento: This turn, we are launching a major offensive on the weakest enemy outposts: Coimbra and Castellon. We are committing all available troops from Santarem and Valencia to secure these victories. At the same time, we are sending reinforcements to Madrid to support our marching army and eliminate its garrison. We are also reinforcing our borders from our interior villages and building new troops across our empire to ensure we have the resources for the next phase of our campaign.
A.plano: Focus on expanding our borders by attacking the weakest enemy villages first: Coimbra and Castellon. We are sending our full available forces from Santarem and Valencia to conquer them. Meanwhile, we are sending reinforcements from Toledo and Badajoz to Madrid to follow up on the marching army, aiming to wipe out its garrison and conquer it next turn. We are also reinforcing our border villages from our interior villages to maintain a strong defense.

B.depoimento: The enemy is attacking Madrid, and I'm throwing everything I can at its defense. Sending all troops from Salamanca and Zaragoza as reinforcement waves. Building archers and knights across all 13 villages to rebuild my strength. Last turn's attacks on Valencia and Badajoz both failed — I need to consolidate before striking again.
B.plano: Defending Madrid is the priority this turn — the enemy army arrives in 1 turn. I sent all troops from Salamanca and Zaragoza as layered reinforcement waves. Building archers and knights everywhere to grow my army for next turn. Next turn: if Madrid holds, attack weak targets like Toledo (from Madrid or Zaragoza) and Badajoz (from Salamanca/Porto). Keep Burgos as reserve force. Must not lose more villages.

A.depoimento: This turn, we launched a major offensive against the weak enemy villages of Porto and Salamanca, sending our full available forces from Coimbra and Badajoz. We also reinforced our borders by sending troops from Santarem, Faro, Sevilha, and Toledo to Coimbra and Badajoz. Our economy is focused on building knights in almost all villages to strengthen our army. We hope to conquer Porto and Salamanca next turn and push towards Madrid.
A.plano: We are focusing on expanding our borders by conquering the weak enemy villages of Porto and Salamanca. We are sending our full forces from Coimbra and Badajoz to attack them. Simultaneously, we are reinforcing our border villages from our interior villages to maintain a strong defense and prepare for future enemy counterattacks. We are also building knights in almost all our villages to grow our army for the next turns.

B.depoimento: King B focuses all his strength on defending Madrid against the incoming enemy army. Reinforcements from Burgos, Zaragoza, Salamanca, and Huesca march to Madrid to form an unbreakable wall. Meanwhile, our blacksmiths work overtime, forging knights across the realm to prepare for a decisive counter-offensive next turn.
B.plano: Madrid is under attack this turn. I sent all available troops from Burgos, Zaragoza, Salamanca, and Huesca to reinforce Madrid, creating a massive defense stack. I built knights in almost all villages to grow my mobile strike force. Next turn, if Madrid holds, I will launch counter-attacks from Madrid against Toledo, and from Porto/Salamanca against Coimbra/Badajoz. I must watch for enemy reinforcements and protect my border villages.

B.depoimento: King B's forces moved on multiple fronts. Madrid sent a large reinforcement to Salamanca to repel the enemy assault, while a detachment captured Toledo. Tarragona's army took Castellon. Reinforcements from Girona and Barcelona flowed into Tarragona to secure the new border. Troops from the interior marched to strengthen the capital Madrid and the approaches. All villages produced new troops. The king's strategy is expanding while holding the line.
B.plano: This turn we defended Salamanca by sending 25 archers and 4 knights from Madrid. We attacked Toledo with 5 archers and 1 knight, and Castellon with 12 archers and 2 knights from Tarragona. We reinforced Tarragona with troops from Girona and Barcelona, and moved troops from Zaragoza, Huesca, Pamplona, and Burgos to strengthen Madrid and its approaches. We also sent some troops from Vigo to Porto and from Porto to Salamanca. We built one unit in every village. Next turn, we will check the battle results, continue building, and plan attacks on Coimbra, Badajoz, and Teruel.

A.depoimento: I am building up my forces, focusing on knights to counter the enemy's archers. I am sending reinforcements to Badajoz and Valencia to launch attacks on Toledo and Castellon next turn. I am leaving minimal troops in the interior to protect my home villages while I concentrate on the borders.
A.plano: Focus on building knights to counter enemy archers. Reinforce Badajoz and Valencia for next turn's attacks on Toledo and Castellon. Leave minimal troops in interior villages for defense. Attack Toledo with knights/archers from Badajoz, and Castellon with knights from Valencia next turn.

B.depoimento: Our armies took Valencia and Coimbra, expanding our realm to 15 villages. Reinforcements marched to Toledo to secure the southern front. The interior provinces emptied their garrisons to support the border, and every village produced new troops. The march continues.
B.plano: We attacked Valencia and Coimbra this turn, bringing our total to 15 villages. We reinforced Toledo from Madrid to prepare for the next attack on Cordoba. We moved troops from the interior to the borders to support these attacks and built troops in all villages. Next turn, we will check the status of Toledo (risk of attack from Badajoz), and plan attacks on Cordoba and Badajoz. We will also consider attacking Teruel from the east. We must ensure we hold our new villages and continue building.

A.depoimento: I launched a major assault on Toledo from Badajoz, sending my entire army. I reinforced my borders by sending troops to Santarem and Valencia, and I sent reinforcements to Badajoz to replenish its ranks. I focused on building knights to counter the enemy's archers. I am confident we are making progress towards victory.
A.plano: I attacked Toledo with all troops from Badajoz to secure the center. I reinforced Santarem from Lisboa and Valencia from Murcia for next turn's attacks on Coimbra and Castellon. I also sent reinforcements from Sevilha and Faro to Badajoz to rebuild it. I built knights in Lisboa, Santarem, Sevilha, Valencia, Murcia and archers elsewhere. Next turn, I will attack Coimbra from Santarem and Castellon from Valencia, and check on Toledo.

B.depoimento: Today, I ordered a simultaneous assault on four enemy strongholds—Valencia, Cordoba, Badajoz, and Santarem—striking at the heart of King A's territory. I committed nearly all of our frontline archers and knights, leaving our border villages temporarily stripped of their garrisons but trusting in the speed of our offensive to secure the victory. In tandem, I marched reinforcements from our interior cities to our key staging grounds, ensuring the spearhead remains sharp. Our forges burned day and night, producing a fresh cohort of archers and knights to fill the ranks of the wounded. The battle
B.plano: We launched a four-front attack on Valencia, Cordoba, Badajoz, and Santarem using almost all border troops. We reinforced Toledo, Castellon, and Coimbra from the interior. We built archers and knights everywhere. Next turn, we must check the battle results. If we conquered these 4 villages, we will have 18 villages total, which is 75% of the map. We must then secure the new borders and build up troops there. We should also consider attacking Teruel if it is still neutral and we need more villages. Do not leave the newly conquered villages undefended.
